scenarios.title: Someone Is Choking
scenarios.description: A friend at dinner suddenly can't speak or cough, and is clutching their throat. Their face is turning red.

choices.feedback: Correct. When someone can't speak, cough, or breathe, their airway is fully blocked. Abdominal thrusts above the navel can dislodge the object and clear the airway.

choices.text: Give them water to help wash it down
choices.feedback: Giving liquid to someone with a blocked airway can make things worse and won't clear the obstruction. Only act on the airway itself, not by adding more to swallow.

choices.text: Wait to see if they can clear it on their own
choices.feedback: A fully blocked airway cuts off oxygen within minutes. If someone can't speak, cough, or breathe, act immediately rather than waiting.

scenarios.title: Severe Bleeding from a Cut
scenarios.description: Someone has cut their arm badly on broken glass, and blood is flowing steadily from the wound.

choices.text: Apply firm, steady direct pressure with a clean cloth
choices.feedback: Correct. Direct, continuous pressure is the most effective way to control bleeding while waiting for medical help. If blood soaks through, add another layer rather than removing the first.

choices.text: Lift the cloth every minute to check if the bleeding stopped
choices.feedback: Lifting the cloth breaks up any clot that's starting to form and restarts the bleeding. Keep steady pressure on and add more layers instead of checking underneath.

choices.text: Rinse the wound thoroughly with water first
choices.feedback: Washing a severely bleeding wound can wash away clotting and increase blood loss. Focus on stopping the bleeding first; cleaning comes later with medical care.

scenarios.title: Kitchen Burn
scenarios.description: Someone accidentally touches a hot pan and burns their hand. The skin is red and starting to sting badly.

choices.text: Run the burn under cool (not ice-cold) running water for about 20 minutes
choices.feedback: Correct. Cooling a burn under running water reduces skin temperature and limits damage. Twenty minutes is the generally recommended duration for minor burns.

choices.text: Apply butter or oil to soothe the burn
choices.feedback: Butter, oil, and toothpaste trap heat against the skin and can worsen the burn and increase infection risk. Cool running water is the correct first response.

choices.text: Cover the burn immediately with a tight bandage
choices.feedback: Cooling the burn should come first. Wrapping it tightly right away traps heat and can increase swelling and pain before the area has had a chance to cool.
